blocking_findings: Double word space for an in-tree run-in rubric that comes right before an inline conditional (reledmac.xslt:4034-4045). Take `<tei:p><tei:note type="instruction">Rubric</tei:note><j:conditional type="marked" .../>inside…`, which is the ordinary non-parallel case where the original note is emitted. Two blocks fire. (1) The existing run-in separator at 4034-4038 fires: $within, not $crosses, and not parallel-block are all true. following-sibling::node()[string(.) ne ''][1] skips the empty j:conditional milestone and lands on 'inside'. If the conditional carries a tei:note child, it lands on the conditional's own string instead, which normally starts with a letter. Either way it matches ^[\p{L}\p{N}\p{Ps}] and emits '\ '. (2) The new block at 4041-4045 also fires, through its second disjunct ($within and following-sibling::node()[1] is an inline j:conditional), and emits a second '\ '. Two control spaces give two interword glues. TeX does not collapse them. The same thing happens in the copied path whenever the copy still has a following non-empty text sibling. The stamped f:before-inline-condition='true' then fires block 2 while block 1 fires on the remaining text. The new geometry test cannot catch this: it covers only the parallel copy, and pdftotext prints a doubled interword gap as one space, so 'Rubric [inside]' passes either way. Fix: emit at most one space, e.g. `<xsl:if test="$command = 'instructionnote' and (@f:before-inline-condition = 'true' or ($within and following-sibling::node()[1]/self::j:conditional[...])) and not(<the 4034 condition>)">`. Or compute one boolean and emit '\ ' once. Add a TeX-level assertion for both the in-tree and the copied fixture: exactly one '\ ' after the \instructionnote{…} closing brace, or no '\ \ ' sequence. Also add an in-tree rendered case with a bbox gap check against a normal interword gap.
nonblocking_findings: Full-width f:head path (reledmac.xslt:2499) is acceptable. The order is \pend [line-list writes] \par (a no-op in vertical mode) \OSApplyKeep \vskip0.5\baselineskip, then \begingroup\pstart. When a keep is pending, the \nobreak sits directly before the new glue, so the glue is not a breakpoint. The \pstart hook's \OSApplyKeep then finds the flag already cleared, and its \vspace follows glue, so that is not a breakpoint either. Keep-with-previous-rubric therefore still holds, and \OSKeepNext after \pend\endgroup still governs the following paragraph. With no keep pending, the glue follows the \pend whatsits and is an ordinary legal break. It is discarded at a page top: whatsits do not make the page non-empty, so it is still dropped there. This applies only to the non-$single-pstart stream, so reledpar pstart pairing is unaffected, and the $single-pstart branch is unchanged as stated.

Spanning heading path (reledmac.xslt:1085-1098) is fine. The inner \par after \begin{hebrew} is a no-op in vertical mode, \nobreak is followed directly by \vskip (not a legal break), and \noindent then starts the title paragraph explicitly inside the group, with \parfillskip=0pt still in effect. Note that the 0.5\baselineskip adds to whatever separation the preceding \pend or \Columns material already leaves. If headings that follow a block rule or section separator now look too loose, consider \addvspace semantics or a conditional skip. That is cosmetic.

The new f:before-inline-condition stamp (reledmac.xslt:3208-3210) tests following-sibling::node()[1] strictly. Pretty-printed whitespace between the note and the conditional therefore turns it off, which is correct because the source space survives.

The negative control is good evidence for the copied-rubric and full-width-heading fixes: both fail on 1e4bed4 and pass now. It does not cover the in-tree non-parallel rubric+conditional case, which is where the blocker above lives.
limitations: This was a static review of the XSLT around the changed hunks and the provided logs. I did not run XSLT, lualatex or pytest. I have inferred the double space from the XPath conditions. I did not observe it in TeX output. Possible exception: if the emit template only ever gets stamped copies that have no siblings, the second disjunct is dead code and the in-tree case cannot occur. A one-line transform of the in-tree fixture would settle this.

I did not check what \pstart and \AtEveryPstart* emit internally beyond the preamble comments (lines 300-319). My keep analysis assumes, as those comments say, that the hook runs directly before \pstart's \vspace and that no whatsit comes between them.
The final full affected-test run is still in progress and is not covered. Proof images were reviewed separately and are not covered here.
